purpose: Durable M4 #245 public reduction dispatch acceptance corpus. The first seven cases retain the original authored IDs and source expressions byte-for-byte; three independently captured source-order cases supplement them.

portable_reference.status: ClojureScript raw observations are pinned; all ten cases have since matched native Runtime and Macro observations in the focused working-tree run.

source_guidance.use: Ordinary reduce two- and three-argument collection coverage guidance only; the upstream file explicitly leaves Reduced to separate tests.
Existing pinned early-termination, Reduced, empty and singleton cases; guidance, not copied expected observations.
Existing bounded collection-reduction and callback-stop shape.

Source classification only: PersistentArrayMap and PersistentHashMap implement IKVReduce. PersistentHashSet (type body around lines 4375-4460) and PersistentQueue (type body around lines 5626-5695) have no IReduce declaration, and no IReduce extension for either was found; their ordinary reduce cases exercise sequence fallback, not a type-optimized route. No source is copied.

cases.source: (let [run (fn [m] (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce-kv (fn [acc k v] (swap! seen conj [k v]) (+ acc v)) 0 m)] [result @seen (instance? PersistentArrayMap m) (instance? PersistentHashMap m)]))] [(run array-map-source) (run hamt-source)])
cases.host_validation: Each nested result has the expected sum, and its raw callback pairs contain every input entry exactly once. Canonicalize/decode pairs on the host and compare membership without requiring traversal order; do not deduplicate guest-side. Exactly one public representation predicate is true.

cases.source: (let [run (fn [m] (let [calls (atom 0) result (reduce-kv (fn [acc _k _v] (swap! calls inc) acc) 17 m)] [result @calls (instance? PersistentArrayMap m) (instance? PersistentHashMap m)]))] [(run array-map-empty) (run hamt-empty)])
cases.host_validation: Both return the initial value with zero callback calls; representation is verified only with public instance? checks.

cases.source: (let [run (fn [m] (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce-kv (fn [_acc k v] (swap! seen conj [k v]) (reduced :stopped)) 0 m)] [result @seen (instance? PersistentArrayMap m) (instance? PersistentHashMap m)]))] [(run array-map-source) (run hamt-source)])
cases.host_validation: Each result is :stopped and has exactly one raw callback pair; that pair belongs to the full corresponding reference input map. Accept whichever key the implementation visits first; do not assert CLJS traversal order. This calls public reduce-kv, unlike macro-map-cases.json/kv-reduce, which calls -kv-reduce directly.

cases.source: (let [sum-entry (fn [acc entry] (+ (if (number? acc) acc (val acc)) (val entry)))] [(reduce sum-entry record-source) (reduce sum-entry 0 record-source) (instance? ReductionDispatchRecord record-source)])
cases.host_validation: Both public reduce forms sum the declared record values; verify the public record type without inspecting or stripping compiler/test source.

cases.source: (let [trace2 (atom []) trace3 (atom []) r2 (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! trace2 conj x) (+ acc x)) queue-source) r3 (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! trace3 conj x) (+ acc x)) 0 queue-source)] [r2 @trace2 r3 @trace3 (instance? PersistentQueue queue-source)])
cases.host_validation: Both forms sum to 10. Require exact FIFO callback traces: [2 3 4] for no-init and [1 2 3 4] with init. The instance? result confirms only the public concrete type, not an IReduce-optimized dispatch path.

cases.source: (let [seen2 (atom []) seen3 (atom []) r2 (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! seen2 conj x) (+ acc x)) set-source) r3 (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! seen3 conj x) (+ acc x)) 0 set-source)] [r2 (count @seen2) @seen2 r3 (count @seen3) @seen3 (instance? PersistentHashSet set-source)])
cases.host_validation: Both forms sum to 10. Host-decode raw callback inputs, then compare order-independently: no-init has any three unique inputs from the full four-element reference input; init has all four. Do not require the reference implementation's exact omitted seed or iteration order, and do not deduplicate guest-side. The instance? result confirms only PersistentHashSet representation; source has no IReduce implementation, so this is sequence-fallback coverage.

cases.source: (let [record2 (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce (fn [acc entry] (swap! seen conj [acc entry]) (reduced :stopped)) record-source)] [result @seen]) record3 (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce (fn [acc entry] (swap! seen conj [acc entry]) (reduced :stopped)) :seed record-source)] [result @seen]) queue2 (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! seen conj x) (reduced :stopped)) queue-source)] [result @seen]) queue3 (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! seen conj x) (reduced :stopped)) :seed queue-source)] [result @seen]) set2 (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! seen conj [acc x]) (reduced :stopped)) set-source)] [result @seen]) set3 (let [seen (atom []) result (reduce (fn [acc x] (swap! seen conj [acc x]) (reduced :stopped)) :seed set-source)] [result @seen])] [record2 record3 queue2 queue3 set2 set3])
cases.host_validation: Each of the six results unwraps to :stopped and records exactly one callback effect, proving no later callback ran. For record, preserve raw accumulator/entry pairs and validate against the complete reference record sequence without inferring JVM order. For queue, require exact FIFO traces: [2] without init and [1] with init. For set, validate raw callback input membership against the full four-element reference set; for no-init the pair contains two distinct set members, while with init the input is one member. Never assert set iteration order. Queue/set representation checks are not evidence of optimized IReduce dispatch; source shows sequence fallback.

independent_decoder_policy: Capture and decode raw runtime values independently in the native harness; preserve map keys and callback arguments. Perform canonical unordered comparisons on the host only. Do not use guest-computed equality as proof of the reference result.
